scenario: AITA for telling my SIL to shut up? | My SIL drives me a little bonkers sometimes. She is extremely proud of things like not watching TV, not listening to pop music, not having Facebook, and she interrupts conversations to say it. Often insulting the thing as well, instead of just saying that she doesn’t like it. Instead it’s about her superiority for not liking it. A few days ago we were having dinner and my 14-year-old sister starts talking about she watched a Marvel movie and she’s looking forward to a sequel that should be coming out soon. My SIL said, “I’ve never watched any Marvel movies. They seem pretty awful.” I was pissed off, I don’t get why my SIL, an adult woman, feels the need to be so rude and dismissive towards a teenager. I said loudly, “shut up, not everything has to be about you and what you like.” She blushed and didn’t say anything more, my brother didn’t say anything either. But he messaged me after they left saying that this was my expression of “always hating” his wife and that I’m a bad person who doesn’t want her to participate in conversation. AITA?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me to tell my SIL (sister-in-law) to shut up during dinner. Let me start by understanding the situation better. My SIL is someone who is really proud of not watching TV, not listening to pop music, and not having Facebook. She often interrupts conversations to mention these things, and instead of just saying she doesn't like them, she makes it about her superiority for not liking them. A few days ago, during dinner, my 14-year-old sister started talking about a Marvel movie she watched and was looking forward to the sequel. My SIL interrupted and said she had never watched any Marvel movies and that they seemed pretty awful. I got really upset because I don't understand why my SIL feels the need to be so rude and dismissive towards a teenager. So, I loudly told her to shut up, saying that not everything has to be about her and what she likes. She blushed and didn't say anything more, and my brother didn't say anything either. But later, he messaged me saying that this was my expression of always hating his wife and that I'm a bad person who doesn't want her to participate in conversations. Now, I'm wondering if I did the right thing or not. On one hand, I felt like my SIL was being rude and dismissive towards my sister, and I wanted to stand up for her. On the other hand, telling someone to shut up is pretty harsh, and it might have made things worse between me and my SIL, especially since my brother is upset with me now. I also need to consider the dynamics of the family. My brother is married to my SIL, so he might be more defensive of her, which could explain why he's upset with me. I should think about how my actions affected not just the immediate situation but also the broader family relationships. Maybe I should have handled the situation differently. Instead of telling her to shut up, perhaps I could have addressed her behavior more calmly or found a way to redirect the conversation. That way, I could have stood up for my sister without escalating the situation. I also need to reflect on why my SIL behaves this way. Is she insecure? Does she feel the need to assert her superiority in some areas? Understanding her motivations might help me respond more effectively in the future. Additionally, I should consider the impact of my actions on my sister. While I stood up for her, the way I did it might have made her uncomfortable or set a negative example. It's important to balance standing up for someone with maintaining respectful communication. In the end, I think it's important to approach such situations with empathy and calmness. While it's natural to feel upset when someone is dismissive, reacting harshly can lead to more conflict and strained relationships. Finding a constructive way to address the issue might be a better approach in the future.
